ruling.recommended_action: Close the dispute as no refund; no driver action and no RD-7 reminder (rider agreed to the route before the segment). Log the case against the rider's existing refund-claim pattern for Trust & Safety visibility only — no account action.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip ran 30.0 km against a 24.4 km optimal route, and the billed excess is 5.54 km over the 1 km tolerance, so the case is in scope for RD-1 / RD-2 [F1][F4][RD-1]. The whole deviation sits in one off-route segment, 18:44–18:55, which drove 7.35 km where the optimal route covers 2.38 km, adding 4.97 km [F3].

Consent and its scope turn on the words before the segment. At 18:41 the driver asked "Traffic ahead on Ayer Rajah Expressway is building up, shall I take another way?" [F7], and at 18:42 — before the 18:44 segment start — the rider replied "Just take whichever way is faster lah, I'm late" [F8], an acknowledgement of a general route choice under RD-5 [F8][RD-5]. The words name no road (the only road named, the Ayer Rajah Expressway, was the one to be avoided), so the named-road branch does not arise; the driver's later statement that the rider said any faster way was fine adds nothing, because a driver's statement is not consent [F10][RD-5].

The only remaining question is whether that general consent reaches this segment. A general route choice covers the route chosen to get there; it stops covering a stop away from the route or a loop of the driver's own that reaches nothing. On this record the segment is a continuous drive toward the destination — Clementi West Street 1, West Coast Road, Clementi Road, Kent Ridge Crescent and Drive, Arts Link, Computing Drive, Heng Mui Keng Terrace, Pasir Panjang Road, South Buona Vista Road — every road lying on the western corridor between Jurong Point and Suntec City [F3]. Nothing in the record shows a stop, an errand, or a detour to an off-route destination the rider did not name; no RD-3 stop is measured in the segment [F3][RD-3]. The segment therefore falls on the general-consent side of RD-5 and is exempt [F8][F3][RD-5].

The rider's "it wasn't faster" argument (37.3 min actual against a 33.6 min estimate) goes to the merit of the chosen corridor, not to the scope of the consent: RD-4 is settled on the record — the Ayer Rajah Expressway the driver asked to leave was at speed band 2 (10–19 km/h) and congested from 18:23 to 18:55, already active when the segment began and still active during it [F11][RD-4]. RD-2's "traffic reason, rider informed and agreed" row therefore applies to the informed decision to leave that road, and the general consent in F8 was the rider's own route choice [F7][F8][F11][RD-2].

With the 4.97 km segment exempt, what remains is 5.54 km − 4.97 km = 0.57 km, which is at or under the 1 km tolerance, so no refund is due [F4][F3][RD-1][RD-2]; amount = (5.54 − 4.97) × $1.4099 = $0.80, rounded and already within tolerance, hence no_action with amount null.

On the profile facts: neither party has an upheld route dispute in 90 days, so RD-6 is checked and not satisfied — no flag_account [F17][RD-6]. The rider's fraud-flag count [F16] is never cited here because profile facts never decide the case on their own, and it is not a basis for the outcome. The evidence is complete — the segment's times and roads are recorded, and every chat message is timestamped — so nothing needs escalation under TH-4 [F3][F9][TH-4].

The segment drove a continuous corridor toward Suntec City; the record shows no stop, errand or off-route destination of the driver's own, so the general consent covers the segment and it is exempt [RD-5].

rejected_claims.reason: RD-4's traffic screen is settled by the record: the Ayer Rajah Expressway on the recommended route was at band 2 (10–19 km/h) and congested from 18:23 to 18:55, active before and during the segment [F11], so the 'no traffic reason' reading fails; RD-4 does not require the congested road to appear among the roads driven [RD-4].

The rider's consent covers the route chosen to get there; a longer-than-estimated duration (37.3 min vs 33.6 min) [F2] does not undo a general route choice, and the record shows no driver's errand or off-route destination in the segment [F3][F8][RD-5].

The refund computation fails because the segment is exempt: 5.54 km deviation − 4.97 km exempt = 0.57 km, at or under the 1 km tolerance, so no excess distance fare is refundable [F3][F4][RD-1][RD-2].

A refund request under $10 may be decided by the system under TH-1, but the merits here yield no refundable excess after the RD-5 exemption, so the ruling is no_action, not refund_partial [F3][F4][RD-2].

The driver's reading reaches the right ground (general_route_consent) but his stated basis that the whole 4.97 km is automatically covered is accepted only because this record shows no stop or errand; the exemption rests on the absence of any driver's own detour destination [F3][F8], not on the bare fact of a short yes [RD-3][RD-5].

The traffic-reason row of RD-2 is established [F11], but the outcome for an exempt segment is no refund because the residual deviation (0.57 km) is within tolerance, not because a traffic reroute automatically excuses all km [F3][RD-1][RD-2].
The driver's post-trip statement [F10] is not treated as consent, and RD-6 is not satisfied in any event since no route deviation is upheld against him [F17][RD-6].
